name: David Dobrik
milestone_by_age_26: Amassed over one million followers on Vine by age 17 and launched his self-titled YouTube vlog channel at age 19, growing to 15M+ subscribers by age 23.
early_history_summary: Dobrik immigrated to the US from Slovakia at age 6 and grew up in suburban Chicago. He discovered Vine in 2013 at age 17, initially running sports highlight accounts before transitioning to comedic content, and moved to Los Angeles after high school to pursue content creation full-time.
family_context_summary: Born in Košice, Slovakia to a Slovak father and Hungarian mother; family immigrated to Vernon Hills, Illinois when he was six. No evidence of significant family wealth or media industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Vine early adopter, LA relocation, Vlog Squad collaborators, immigrant hustle
evidence_summary: Dobrik started on Vine at 17 in 2013, building sports highlight accounts before pivoting to comedy. He amassed over a million Vine followers and launched his YouTube vlog in 2015 at age 19, growing to 15M+ subscribers by 2019. His early advantage was timing the Vine platform wave and moving to LA to collaborate with other creators. No evidence of family wealth or industry connections; his success was self-created through platform-native content and the Vlog Squad collaborative format.
starting_point: Born to a Slovak father and Hungarian mother in Košice, Slovakia; family immigrated to a middle-class suburb of Chicago when he was six years old.
current_position: Active YouTuber with ~17M subscribers; estimated peak net worth ~$25M; resides in Los Angeles; career disrupted by 2021 Vlog Squad controversies but returned to posting in 2025.

trajectory.event: Uploaded first Vine video and began building sports highlight accounts, eventually amassing over one million followers.
Launched self-titled YouTube vlog channel, pioneering the fast-paced vlog format with the Vlog Squad.
Named Generation Z's favorite social media personality by Piper Saffray survey; surpassed 15M YouTube subscribers.
Faced major backlash from Vlog Squad sexual assault allegations; lost brand deals and stepped back from YouTube.
Returned to active YouTube content creation after a multi-year hiatus.

name: Ashraf Marwan
milestone_by_age_26: Began working in the Egyptian Presidential Office in 1968 at age 24, serving as a close aide to President Nasser and later President Sadat.
early_history_summary: Born into an elite Egyptian family — his grandfather was chief of Sharia courts and his father a major general in the military — Marwan graduated from Cairo University in 1965 with a chemical engineering degree. He married President Nasser's daughter Mona in 1966, which accelerated his rise into the inner circle of Egyptian power.
family_context_summary: Born into a prominent Egyptian family in Cairo; grandfather was chief of Sharia courts, father was a major general and deputy commander of the Republican Guard, mother belonged to the prominent al-Fayyad family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a senior military officer (major general) who served as deputy commander of the Republican Guard, providing direct exposure to Egypt's military-political elite from birth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: military family, presidential marriage, elite Cairo networks, Republican Guard connections
evidence_summary: Marwan was born into Egypt's military-judicial elite: his grandfather led the Sharia courts and his father was a major general in the Republican Guard. He graduated from Cairo University in 1965, married President Nasser's daughter in 1966, and entered the Presidential Office in 1968 at age 24. His trajectory was almost entirely driven by inherited family networks and the strategic marriage into the ruling family, which gave him direct access to the highest levels of Egyptian power.
starting_point: Born into an elite Cairo family; grandfather was chief of Sharia courts and father was a major general serving as deputy commander of the Republican Guard.
current_position: Died in 2007 at age 63 after falling from the balcony of his London home under mysterious circumstances; final role was arms dealer and businessman living in London.

trajectory.event: Graduated from Cairo University with a chemical engineering degree and began working in Egypt's military industry as a second lieutenant.
Married Mona Nasser, daughter of President Gamal Abdel Nasser, gaining entry into Egypt's ruling family.
Started working in the Presidential Office under Nasser's aide-de-camp Sami Sharaf, entering the inner circle of Egyptian power.
Became a close aide to Nasser's successor, Anwar Sadat, and helped defuse an attempted coup in 1971.
Appointed head of the Arab Industrialisation Organisation, a major Arab-financed arms development project.
Moved to London and became an arms dealer and businessman.
Died after falling from the balcony of his London home under mysterious circumstances; suspected of being a double agent.

name: Daniela Silivaș
milestone_by_age_26: Won gold on balance beam at the 1985 World Championships at age 13, then became the star of the 1988 Olympics with six medals (three gold) at age 16.
early_history_summary: Silivaș began gymnastics at age 6 in Deva, Romania, and was coached by Béla Károlyi before his defection. She was Romanian junior national champion at ages 9-10 and won three medals at the 1984 Junior European Championships at age 12, establishing herself as a world-class gymnast before her teens.
family_context_summary: Born in Deva, Romania, the site of Romania's national gymnastics training center. Family background not extensively documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Deva training center, Károlyi coaching, Romanian gymnastics system, early specialization, junior champion
evidence_summary: Silivaș started gymnastics at age 6 in Deva, home of Romania's national gymnastics training center, and was coached by Béla Károlyi. She was junior national champion by age 9, won three medals at the 1984 Junior European Championships at 12, and won World Championship gold on balance beam at 13 in 1985. Her path was defined by Romania's elite gymnastics pipeline, early specialization, and world-class coaching. Her birth year was falsified by Romanian authorities to make her eligible for the 1985 World Championships.
starting_point: Born in Deva, Romania, the city that housed Romania's national gymnastics training center; family background not extensively documented.
current_position: Retired from competitive gymnastics in 1991; moved to the United States and works as a gymnastics coach; living in the Atlanta, Georgia area.

trajectory.event: Won the Romanian junior national championship, establishing herself as a gymnastics prodigy.
Won gold on balance beam and silver on uneven bars and floor at the Junior European Championships.
Won gold on balance beam at the World Championships in Montréal, becoming a world champion before age 14.
Won six medals at the Seoul Olympics (three gold, two silver, one bronze), medaling in every event.
Won three gold medals at the World Championships despite a serious knee injury.
Retired from competitive gymnastics and eventually emigrated to the United States.

name: Ismael "El Mayo" Zambada
milestone_by_age_26: No specific, dated, material milestone by age 26 found. Zambada reportedly entered the drug trade at age 16 in the early 1960s but his rise to a major cartel leadership role occurred in the 1980s and 1990s, well after age 26.

name: Cristian Gațu
milestone_by_age_26: Won World Championship bronze with Romania in 1967 at age 22 and World Championship gold in 1970 at age 25, establishing himself as one of the world's best handball players before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Bucharest to a sports journalist father, Gațu began playing football at age 7 at Dinamo's youth academy. He switched to handball at age 18 in 1963 and debuted for the Romanian national team the following year, quickly becoming a world-class player despite starting the sport late.
family_context_summary: Born in Bucharest to parents who were both journalists; his father was a sports journalist specializing in football who introduced him to sports from age 3.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a sports journalist specializing in football who took Gațu to stadiums from age 5, providing early immersion in the sports world and connections to major clubs like Dinamo.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Dinamo youth system, sports journalist father, Romanian handball golden generation, Steaua Bucharest
evidence_summary: Gațu was born to a sports journalist father who introduced him to football at age 5, enrolling him at Dinamo's youth academy by age 7. He switched to handball at 18 in 1963 and debuted for the national team within a year. He won World Championship bronze at 22 in 1967 and gold at 25 in 1970, benefiting from Romania's elite handball pipeline and his father's sports world connections. His late switch to handball was catalyzed by a football disappointment but his all-around athletic foundation enabled rapid mastery.
starting_point: Born in Bucharest to parents who were both journalists; father was a sports journalist who introduced him to football and the sports world from age 3.
current_position: Retired from competitive handball in 1977; served as president of the Romanian Handball Federation from 1997 to 2014; currently retired and living in Romania at age 80.

trajectory.event: Switched from football to handball and debuted for the Romanian national team within a year.
Won World Championship bronze with Romania in Sweden.
Won World Championship gold with Romania in France, establishing himself as the world's best handball player.
Won Olympic bronze medal with Romania at the Munich Games.
Won his second World Championship gold with Romania in East Germany.
Won Olympic silver medal with Romania at the Montreal Games.
Retired from competitive handball after winning the European Champions Cup with Steaua Bucharest.
Became president of the Romanian Handball Federation, a position he held until 2014.

name: Sergei Magnitsky
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Magnitsky won a physics Olympiad at 15 and attended the Plekhanov Institute, but his defining work — exposing a $230M tax fraud by Russian officials — occurred in 2007-2008 at age 35-36, leading to his arrest and death in custody in 2009.

name: Padma Bandopadhyay
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Bandopadhyay graduated from the Armed Forces Medical College in 1967 and joined the IAF in 1968 at age 24, but her first major recognition — the Vishisht Seva Medal for conduct during the 1971 war — came at age 27. Her historic firsts (first woman Air Marshal, first woman DSSC graduate) occurred in her 30s-50s.

name: Szymon Marciniak
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Marciniak began refereeing at age 21 in 2002 but his first top-league match came in 2009 at age 28. His major achievements — World Cup final 2022, Champions League final 2023, World's Best Referee 2022-2023 — all came after age 35.

name: Monkey Punch
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Monkey Punch made his professional manga debut in 1965 at age 28 with Playboy School, and Lupin III — his defining work — debuted in August 1967 at age 30. No significant professional publication is documented before age 26.

name: Anton Zeilinger
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found. Zeilinger received his PhD from the University of Vienna in 1971 at age 26, which is a standard academic degree rather than a material independently verifiable milestone. His groundbreaking quantum entanglement work — GHZ states, quantum teleportation, Bell inequality tests — came in the 1990s-2000s, and the Nobel Prize in 2022 at age 77.

name: Efren Reyes
milestone_by_age_26: Recognized as the best pool player in Manila by age 15 and the most notorious billiards player in the Philippines by his mid-teens, with multiple independent sources confirming his dominance in money matches from age 9 onward.
early_history_summary: Born into poverty in Pampanga, Philippines, Reyes was sent at age 5 to live with his uncle who owned a pool hall in Manila. He began playing at age 8, standing on Coca-Cola crates to reach the table, and played his first money match at 9. By 12 he won a $100 tournament, and by 15 he was considered the best pool player in the Philippines.
family_context_summary: Born into poverty in Angeles, Pampanga, as the fifth of nine children; family lived without electricity or running water. Sent to live with his uncle in Manila at age 5, where he cleaned a pool hall and slept on pool tables.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; his uncle owned a pool hall which provided incidental access but no documented coaching or domain mentorship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, pool hall access, self-taught, gambling culture, extreme early reps
evidence_summary: Reyes was born into extreme poverty in Pampanga and sent to live with his uncle at age 5, where he slept on pool tables and began playing at 8 using Coca-Cola crates to reach the table. He played his first money match at 9, won $100 at a tournament at 12, and was recognized as the best pool player in Manila by 15. His path was defined by total immersion in a pool hall environment, extreme practice hours (4+ hours daily from childhood), and the gambling culture that provided constant competitive reps. No formal coaching, no family wealth — his advantage was environmental access and obsessive self-directed practice.
starting_point: Born into poverty in Angeles, Pampanga, Philippines, as the fifth of nine children in a family without electricity or running water; sent to live with his uncle in Manila at age 5.
current_position: Still competing professionally at age 71; widely regarded as the greatest pool player of all time with over 100 international titles; resides in the Philippines.

trajectory.event: Played his first money match at his uncle's pool hall in Manila, beginning a career in competitive pool.
Recognized as the best pool player in Manila and the most notorious billiards player in the Philippines.
Turned professional, beginning to compete in organized tournaments.
Won the U.S. Open Pool Championship, his first major international title.
Defeated Earl Strickland in The Color of Money event, winning $100,000 — the largest single match purse in pool history.
Won the WPA World Nine-ball Championship, becoming a world champion.
Won the World Eight-ball Championship, becoming the first player to win world titles in two different pool disciplines.

name: Igor Zhelezovski
milestone_by_age_26: Set a 1500m world record in March 1983 at age 20 and won the World Sprint Speed Skating Championships in 1985 at age 22, beginning a record six-time reign as world sprint champion.
early_history_summary: Born in Orsha, Byelorussian SSR, Zhelezovski grew up where ice only formed on local ponds and lakes. As a teenager he dragged hoses to flood his own skating surface. He trained under coach Nikolai Gapeenko, placed second at the Soviet junior championships at 16, and won silver at the World Junior Championships in 1982 at age 19.
family_context_summary: Born in Orsha, Byelorussian SSR; grew up in a town without proper ice rinks, flooding local ponds to create skating surfaces. Family background not extensively documented beyond mention of a younger brother who also trained but left sport due to illness.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports system, Armed Forces club Minsk, self-made ice rinks, junior national team, physical dominance
evidence_summary: Zhelezovski grew up in Orsha without proper ice rinks, creating his own skating surfaces by flooding ponds as a teenager. He trained under coach Nikolai Gapeenko and joined the Soviet junior national team, winning silver at the World Junior Championships at 19 in 1982. He set a 1500m world record at 20 in 1983 and won the first of his record six World Sprint Championship titles at 22 in 1985. His imposing physical stature (1.86m, 95kg) earned him the nickname 'The Bear from Minsk.' His trajectory was enabled by the Soviet sports pipeline and the Armed Forces sports society in Minsk.
starting_point: Born in Orsha, Byelorussian SSR, a town without proper ice rinks; grew up flooding local ponds to create skating surfaces and trained under a local coach.
current_position: Died on June 12, 2021 at age 58 in Minsk, Belarus; final roles included president of the Belarusian Speed Skating Federation and Belarusian Paralympic Committee (1996-2001).

trajectory.event: Won silver at the World Junior Allround Speed Skating Championships, establishing himself as an international-level competitor.
Set a 1500m world record of 1:54.26 at Medeo, surprising the speed skating world.
Won the first of his record six World Sprint Speed Skating Championships titles.
Broke the 1500m world record again with a time of 1:52.50 at Calgary.
Won Olympic bronze in the 1000m at the Calgary Winter Olympics.
Won his fourth World Sprint Championship title and began a three-year World Cup dominance in the 1000m.
Won Olympic silver in the 1000m at the Lillehammer Winter Olympics, his final Olympic medal.
Died on June 12, 2021 in Minsk, Belarus.
